claims.text: Laser-based directed energy deposition with iterative remelting will produce a finer microstructure in cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed process will produce a more uniform microstructure in AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed process will reduce elemental segregation relative to conventional processing.
The proposed process will reduce residual stress relative to conventional processing.
The proposed process will reduce defect formation relative to conventional processing.
Conventionally additively manufactured or bulk-processed AlCrFeNiSi typically exhibits compositional segregation.
Conventionally additively manufactured or bulk-processed AlCrFeNiSi typically exhibits significant residual thermal stress and associated defects.
Iterative remelting during laser DED can produce rapid solidification in AlCrFeNiSi.
The intervention will produce a finer, equiaxed grain structure.
Rapid solidification minimizes solute diffusion during phase formation.
Minimizing solute diffusion during phase formation reduces elemental segregation.
Rapid solidification reduces residual thermal gradients.
Iterative remelting further refines the AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
Microstructural refinement leads to lower defect density and improved load-bearing capacity.
The proposed process will increase tensile strength by approximately 20–30% relative to conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed process will increase ductility by approximately 20–30% relative to conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi.
The expected mechanical improvements arise from reduced segregation and residual stress.
Heat accumulation during long builds or changes in atmosphere can alter cooling rates enough to limit the hypothesis's applicability.
